prompt: Mia has a broken arm, so she [____] the heavy box. Use the cue: carry.
target_answer: Mia cannot carry the heavy box.

accepted_answers: must not have cleaned the floor

audit.learner_note: The explicit cues make the epistemic deduction answerable, though `must not have` can be harder to distinguish from prohibition scope.
audit.platform_note: A platform should teach the epistemic reading explicitly or contrast it with `can't have`; otherwise the form is somewhat marked.

prompt: The floor is still dirty, so we can conclude that Sam did not clean it earlier. Complete the sentence using the cue (must / not / clean): Sam _____.
target_answer: Sam must not have cleaned the floor.

audit.learner_note: The unfulfilled plan and present dirty state support negative present perfect.

prompt: Maya planned to wash the car today, but it is still dirty. Complete the sentence using the cue (wash): Maya ____ the car.
target_answer: Maya has not washed the car.

audit.learner_note: The requested earlier action and current open state clearly support the target.

prompt: Mia was asked to close the kitchen window, but it is still open. Complete the sentence using the cue “close”: Mia ____ the kitchen window.
target_answer: Mia has not closed the kitchen window.

audit.learner_note: Being driven to work yesterday naturally licenses “did not walk”; the accepted past progressive “was not walking ... yesterday” is awkward and not visibly selected.
audit.platform_note: The context favors a different aspect, so the item is not valid evidence about progressive + past + negation.

prompt: Ben usually walks to work. Yesterday, his car was at the garage, but it was raining, so his sister drove him. Complete the sentence using the cue (walk): Ben ____ to work yesterday.
target_answer: Ben was not walking to work yesterday.

audit.learner_note: If the rain stopped before departure, “did not walk ... when it was raining” is at least as natural as the sole progressive response.
audit.platform_note: The item needs a simultaneous reference event or explicit progressive cue to measure the target row.

prompt: The rain stopped before we left home. Complete the sentence using the cue “walk”: We ____ to the park when it was raining.
target_answer: We were not walking to the park when it was raining.

accepted_answers: Will your friend bring a camera

audit.learner_note: The future plan and lexical cue determine a yes/no question with will.

prompt: Your friend is planning to bring a camera on the trip. Ask about it using the cue “bring a camera”: ____?
target_answer: Will your friend bring a camera?

audit.learner_note: The ride-home need and subject/verb cue clearly select the target question.

prompt: Mia needs a ride home after work. Complete the question using the cue “you / drive her”: ____?
target_answer: Will you drive her home?

audit.learner_note: A late package most directly supports “has not arrived”; nothing visible requires uncertain `may not have arrived`.
audit.platform_note: The item cannot isolate `may` + perfect + negation without a genuine uncertainty cue or explicit modal.

prompt: The package was expected this morning, but it is still not here. Complete the sentence using the cue “arrive”: The package ___.
target_answer: The package may not have arrived.

audit.learner_note: Habitual time phrase and third-person subject transparently cue `makes`.

prompt: Every morning, the boy ___ his bed before breakfast. (make)
target_answer: The boy makes his bed before breakfast.

audit.learner_note: “Every day” and the supplied verb determine the simple-present form.

prompt: Lena has a morning routine. Complete the sentence using the cue "walk": Lena ___ to work every day.
target_answer: Lena walks to work every day.

audit.learner_note: Current TV watching and full sink support the negative present progressive.

prompt: The sink is still full, and Sam is watching TV. Complete the sentence using “wash”: Sam ___ the dishes.
target_answer: Sam is not washing the dishes.

audit.learner_note: Today's bus alternative directly selects “is not walking.”

prompt: Mia usually walks to work, but today she is taking the bus. Complete the sentence: Mia ____ to work today. (walk)
target_answer: Mia is not walking to work today.

audit.learner_note: Permission context, supplied words, and printed suffix determine the response span.

prompt: The room is hot. Ben asks his teacher for permission. Complete the question using the words could, I, and open: _____ the window?
target_answer: Could I open the window?

audit.learner_note: The rule context and explicit MUST/NOT/OPEN cues clearly select the passive prohibition.

prompt: The paint is still wet. Complete the rule: “The door ____ until tomorrow.” Use the cue: MUST / NOT / OPEN.
target_answer: The door must not be opened until tomorrow.

audit.learner_note: A wet floor does not by itself establish why “the door” must not be opened, and several natural rule phrasings are possible.
audit.platform_note: The item needs an explicit access-door relation and modal/verb cue before it measures must + passive + negation.

prompt: The wet floor is dangerous. Complete the rule: The door ___ until the floor is dry.
target_answer: The door must not be opened until the floor is dry.

audit.learner_note: Stopping after five minutes directly supports the negative hour-long duration statement.

prompt: Sam started washing the car an hour ago, but he stopped after five minutes. Complete the sentence: Sam ____ the car for an hour.
target_answer: Sam has not been washing the car for an hour.

audit.learner_note: Children outside with a ball plus “play” and the location suffix cue ongoing activity.

prompt: The children are outside with a ball. Complete the sentence using “play”: The children ____ in the garden.
target_answer: The children are playing in the garden.

audit.learner_note: “Look at Emma” implies a visual that is not stored, although “right now” and the text still make the answer recoverable.
audit.platform_note: Either attach an image/stimulus or replace the deictic phrase; the core cloze is sound.

prompt: Look at Emma in the kitchen right now. Complete the sentence using the verb “wash”: Emma ____ the dishes.
target_answer: Emma is washing the dishes.

accepted_answers: she would not have found the house
she wouldn't have found the house

audit.learner_note: The factual outcome and without-condition clearly support the negative counterfactual.

prompt: Mia had a map, so she found the house. Without the map, [____]. (find)
target_answer: she would not have found the house

accepted_answers: would not have ridden the bus

audit.learner_note: The only-because premise makes the counterfactual result determinate.

prompt: Maya took the bus only because her bike had a flat tire. Complete the sentence using the words in brackets: Without the flat tire, Maya ___ . (ride / the bus)
target_answer: Without the flat tire, Maya would not have ridden the bus.

audit.learner_note: Ability intent and printed object suffix make the can-question span clear.

prompt: You want to know whether Mia is able to carry the box. Complete the question using the words in brackets: ____ the box? (Mia / carry)
target_answer: Can Mia carry the box?

audit.learner_note: Ability intent and subject/verb cues determine the question.

prompt: Your friend wants to know if your sister is able to drive. Complete the question using the words in brackets: ____ (your sister / drive)?
target_answer: Can your sister drive?

audit.learner_note: The not-ready state at arrival and explicit “not finish” cue determine past perfect negative.

prompt: The guests arrived at seven, but the meal was still not ready. Complete the sentence using “not finish”: She ___ dinner when they arrived.
target_answer: She had not finished dinner when they arrived.

audit.learner_note: Offer context, `shall`, and printed suffix clearly determine “Shall I carry.”
audit.platform_note: A plausible question-completion exercise, particularly in British/formal instruction.

prompt: The bags are heavy, and you offer to help. Use “shall” and “carry” to complete the question: _____ the bags for you?
target_answer: Shall I carry the bags for you?

audit.learner_note: The report-completion task is understandable and has a clear answer.
audit.platform_note: Success also requires reported-speech backshift and pronoun change, neither represented in the one-KC Q-row; it is not a pure `would` item.

prompt: Mia said, “I will carry one bag.” Complete the report: Mia said that she _____.
target_answer: Mia said that she would carry one bag.

audit.learner_note: The explicit `shall` instruction makes the answer clear, but “we shall be waiting” is marked in contemporary general use.
audit.platform_note: Potentially useful in a labelled register lesson; otherwise it appears designed for inventory coverage.

prompt: Our train leaves at ten. At nine, we ____ on the platform. Use shall and the verb wait.
target_answer: We shall be waiting on the platform.

audit.learner_note: The explicit in-progress job at nine determines past passive progressive.

prompt: At nine, the workers were still in the middle of the job. Complete the sentence using “paint”: The wall ____.
target_answer: The wall was being painted.

audit.learner_note: Start time and one-hour-later reference clearly select the passive progressive.

prompt: The workers started painting the kitchen at nine. At ten, the kitchen _____. (paint)
target_answer: The kitchen was being painted.

audit.learner_note: Earlier dirtiness and present cleanliness plus the lexical cue support present perfect.

prompt: The dishes were dirty earlier, but they are clean now. Complete the sentence using the words in brackets: The woman _____. (wash the dishes)
target_answer: The woman has washed the dishes.
